speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from mucous membranes, and a rash of tiny red spots called petechiae; have you noticed if this bleeding is spontaneous, meaning it happens without any injury or trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP).

The clinical picture of spontaneous epistaxis, gum bleeding, and petechiae in a 4-year-old is classic for ITP. To confirm this, I need to see your platelet count. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Plates.
